newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in quiet trade on Wednesday, dealers said.

They said the central Reserve Bank had forecast a market surplus of Z$33 million for Wednesday, but had "surprisingly" not indicated any intention of mopping up the excess by way of a treausury bill auction.
Meanwhile, discount houses were selling 91-day treasury bills in the secondary market at 17.50 percent, unchanged from Tuesday, but call money added half a percentage point to 18 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were quoted easier at 18.75 percent (buying) from 19 percent but their selling rate held steady at 18 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were being bought and sold at 18 and 17.65 percent respectively from 18.25 and 17.50 percent the previous day.
Reserve Bank figures showed the market closed with a Z$32.8 million deficit on Tuesday, from a Z$35 million surplus on Monday.
